Nov 19 : Ubisoft expects net bookings of around 250 million euros ($274.1 million) for the third quarter, the French videogame maker's CFO Frederick Duguet said on Thursday. This reflects a lighter content release program than usual and a particularly competitive holiday season. • Ubisoft's second-quarter net bookings fell 20.8 per cent on the year to 388.9 million euros, but were above its guidance of around 370 million euros, helped by sales of "Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced" • The third phase of its cost-reduction program, targeting a fixed cost base of 1.25 billion euros on a run-rate basis by March 2028, was firmly on track, the company said as it confirmed its full-year targets • Ubisoft expects a "significantly" stronger and diversified content pipeline for fiscal 2027-28 and 2028-29, with releases across major brands

LONDON, Nov 19 : Elon Musk's SpaceXSI has filed its defence against a British lawmaker's lawsuit over fake images of her created using the Grok AI platform, arguing that obviously fictitious, AI-generated content cannot breach someone's right to privacy. Jess Asato, a member of Britain's governing Labour Party who has publicly criticised both Musk and Grok, is suing after users generated sexualised images of her, including a video of her "being chloroformed and prepared for a sexual assault". In its written defence, dated October 29, SpaceXSI, part of Musk's SpaceX, denies liability for any alleged breach of Asato's privacy or data protection rights. Asato filed her lawsuit at London's High Court for misuse of private information and breaches of data protection laws, alleging the way Grok was designed and trained enabled it to generate sexualised content.

The company's defence, in one of the first claims to test liability for the design of an AI system, could provide an insight into how designers may contest similar lawsuits. Lawyers for SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC said it had removed AI-generated images of Asato that breached its terms, including the video depicting Asato being chloroformed. They argued, however, that other images it allowed to remain available "would be understood by reasonable and sensible persons viewing that content to be AI-generated, fictitious and implausible ... rather than as realistic images", meaning Asato has no reasonable expectation of privacy. SpaceXSI also argues it did not breach Asato's data protection rights, including because it "did not determine the content of the relevant users' prompts". LAWMAKER SAYS PLATFORMS SHOULD BE ACCOUNTABLE Asato said in a statement on Thursday that those building powerful AI tools must take responsibility. "SpaceX SI wants to have it both ways," Asato said.  "The company admits it built the AI model, rewrote user requests to add its own graphic details, pulled images from across the internet, and published the results from an account it controls," she said, adding: "Yet it also claims it is a neutral bystander without legal responsibility". Asato is seeking a court order requiring SpaceXSI, which was formerly called xAI and then SpaceXAI, to "implement effective and permanent technical measures" to ensure Grok cannot create manipulated images of her. SpaceXSI says she is not entitled to such an order.  Grok, which is distributed through social media platform X, is subject to regulatory probes in several countries after an outcry over its use to create non-consensual sexualised images. In mid-January, xAI said it restricted image editing in Grok and blocked users from generating images of people in revealing clothing "where it's illegal".  But Reuters found in early February that, even after new curbs, Grok continued to generate sexualised images of people even when users explicitly warned the subjects did not consent. X and xAI did not address detailed questions from Reuters about Grok's generation of sexualised material. In July, xAI sued a man in the US alleging he misused Grok to create child sexual abuse material, in one of the first cases of its kind brought by an AI company.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 19 : Criminal duo Lucia and Jason's blitz through Vice City in "GTA VI" is set to help Take-Two Interactive — the publisher of the blockbuster game that is now a global cultural phenomenon — rake in nearly $2 billion in estimated first-day sales. Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of GTA developer Rockstar Games, is not a household name despite its portfolio of massive hits including the "Red Dead Redemption" franchise and the "NBA 2K" basketball series. Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates total units sold at 19.1 million as of Thursday morning, translating to about $1.84 billion in revenue for Take-Two. That is more than twice the roughly $800 million worth of copies GTA V sold on its first day in 2013, widely regarded as the best-selling videogame in the first 24 hours. Meanwhile, Take-Two has remained tight-lipped about GTA VI demand since it opened for pre-orders in June, limiting commentary to saying demand has been "unprecedented" or "far exceeding expectations."

"The title is so widely anticipated, consumers appear very, very excited, and all the press so far has been universally positive, but we still aren't ready to declare victory," CEO Strauss Zelnick said on Take-Two's earnings call earlier this month. "We tend to avoid claiming success before it occurs." Take-Two shares were down about 1 per cent on Thursday after closing 6 per cent higher in the previous session. GTA VI MARKETING BLITZ Take-Two has shelled out an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs for GTA VI, making it one of the most expensive entertainment projects. Sensor Tower estimates that the game's promotional trailer, GTA VI "Extended Look", on Netflix in August helped drive a sixfold jump in pre-orders. In Miami — which Vice City is based on — the city's NBA team celebrated the release on Wednesday with a Vice City-themed match. Over the weekend, the company is hosting "GTA VI: The Festival" — a music show with a star-studded line-up that includes Grammy-winning rapper Cardi B, hip hop record producer Metro Boomin and rapper Travis Scott. WHAT NEXT FOR TAKE-TWO? Investors have been waiting to hear from Take-Two about its plans for a PC launch of GTA VI and an online version rollout. The online, multiplayer component of a videogame is crucial in turning the title into a recurring revenue engine. Some industry analysts are expecting the PC launch and online mode in 2027. Brokerage TD Cowen named Take-Two one of its 'Best Ideas' for 2027, with its analyst Doug Creutz upbeat about the company's financial prospects when the game releases online. "The potential ceiling for GTA VI's long-term recurrent consumer spending performance is very high ... 'when' and 'how big' the next GTA Online will be is the most important question for the stock, more so than GTA VI unit sales."

Source: Reuters

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 19 : Stocks fell across the world on Thursday as Anthropic's market debut kept trading choppy, while oil prices rose as traders focused on lingering attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Europe's tech stocks and the Nasdaq ebbed and flowed with focus squarely on the Claude developer's IPO. Priced at $83 apiece, valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion, it is the first major AI developer to go public. How it trades in the coming days and weeks will be heavily scrutinized to gauge the broader sentiment towards AI. As of 1635 GMT, Anthropic shares had not yet traded. "We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.97 per cent to 49,710.33, the S&P 500 fell 0.41 per cent to 7,293.42 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.16 points, or 0.01 per cent, to 24,431.04.  MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 0.55 per cent to 1,068.62, and the pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.72 per cent. Emerging market stocks fell 1.28 per cent, while Japan's Nikkei rose 0.71 per cent to 59,444.21. The dollar index was steady after its recent rally to 19-month highs lost momentum. "Dollar bulls are going to need more conviction or more bullish news to drive dollar gains in the short run," Shaun Osborne, chief currency strategist at Scotiabank, said, pointing to a pickup in risk sentiment linked to Anthropic. The index was little changed at 103.81, with the euro up 0.06 per cent at $1.098. OIL EDGES UP In commodities, oil prices edged higher as renewed attacks in the Strait of Hormuz offset a growing view that the oil market will soon be back in surplus. Iran's navy said in a statement carried by state media that two oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and "exploded" on Thursday. Reuters could not independently verify the report. US crude rose 1.25 per cent to $84.30 a barrel and Brent rose to $92.54 per barrel, up 0.64 per cent on the day. Spot gold fell 1.25 per cent to $3,675.99 an ounce, while spot silver fell 1.13 per cent to $44.51 an ounce.

Source: Reuters

Nov 19 : Ahead of Anthropic's blockbuster market debut, brokerages including Needham and Melius Research started coverage of the AI firm with bullish recommendations, betting the company would emerge as the "real AI disruptor". Anthropic was on course to secure a $2 trillion valuation when its shares start trading on Thursday. The stock was set to open at $110.5, 33 per cent higher than the IPO price of $83 per share, according to indications as of 11.38 am ET. Feverish demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff, underscores enduring investor appetite for pure AI plays after enthusiasm for the sector softened in recent weeks. "Anthropic maybe one of the few AI stocks that holds up in the near term, while the rest of the AI trade still faces questions," said Ben Reitzes, analyst at Melius Research, as he started coverage on the stock with a "buy" rating and a 24-month price target of $155.

"Growth opportunities like Anthropic rarely come along, but we think history puts Anthropic in the same dominant bucket as fellow tech titans Amazon, Google and Microsoft," Needham said, as it started coverage with a "buy" rating and a $150 price target. Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google. Both Melius and Citizens, which started coverage with a "market outperform" rating and a $125 price target, expect the firm's revenues to hit over $400 billion by 2029. FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 19 : Anthropic's IPO is having a blockbuster first day following the AI lab's record-setting fundraising. Shares opened more than 30 per cent above their offering price on Thursday at $111.50 a share, conferring a $2 trillion market value - a level exceeded by only a handful of US-listed firms. By reaching that level at the open on Thursday the firm outpaced rival SpaceX, whose value at its opening trade in June hit $1.96 trillion. The company on Wednesday evening priced its offering above range and increased the number of shares being sold, initially valuing the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion and defying concerns about the state of one of the pillars of the artificial intelligence boom. Shares across the AI sector were mixed as investors sift through worries about the impact of higher rates on a sector that took off during the era of easy money, an age that appears to have come to an end.

MARKET REACTION: US STOCKS: Major indexes were mixed after opening higher, with the Nasdaq <.IXIC> up 0.1 per cent  after rising as much as 2 per cent after the open and the S&P 500 down 0.4 per cent after earlier rising nearly 1 per cent. BONDS: US Treasury yields were little changed, with the 2-year yield flat at 4.8 per cent and the 10-year yield flat at 5.066 per cent. FOREX: The dollar index was off 0.03 per cent at 103.79. COMMENTS: TONY, TRZCINKA, SENIOR PORTFOLIO MANAGER, IMPAX ASSET MANAGEMENT, BOSTON: "The market  is looking through this strong IPO.  It doesn’t settle the concerns driving the de-rating of the trade due to changes at Nvidia, (Democratic) blue wave and sentiment in Washington DC."  MICHAEL ROSEN, CIO, ANGELES INVESTMENTS, SANTA MONICA, CALIFORNIA: “The ANT IPO saw strong demand, giving a near-term boost to sentiment in the AI ecosystem. But it doesn’t change some of the fundamental challenges that have arisen with the departure of Jensen Huang at Nvidia or the political pushback on data center, and AI in general, development.“Demand for computing power remains strong, so this is not an industry in imminent collapse, but there is a realignment of marginal winners and losers among investors, and those with existing computing power in a stronger position than those without. So hyperscalers, with strong balance sheets and cash flows may be better positioned than those more exposed to the pure growth of data center buildout.“We continue to emphasize to investors that historically disruptive technological advances favor those companies that can harness the new technology to create new products and services over those that supply the new technology. Some of those beneficiaries will be existing companies that are most adaptable, but many will be entirely new companies that are being started now or are yet to be born. Investors should alter their investment approach to align with the theme of successfully adapting to this disruptive technology.” TALLEY LEGER, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, WEALTH CONSULTING GROUP, KEYPORT, NEW JERSEY: “While Anthropic represents top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure with massive revenue momentum, it isn't a prudent 'buy-at-any-price' opportunity for retail wealth clients . . . We like the enterprise AI narrative, but we do not like overpaying for market sentiment. Patience is a strategy. Let the initial volatility settle, the lock-up period expire, and the company deliver 2–3 quarters of public reporting before establishing a position. . . History shows that retail investors buying hot tech IPOs on day one historically underperform broad market indexes over a 3-year horizon once the initial pop fades.” SHAWN SNYDER, ECONOMIC STRATEGIST, POTOMAC FUND MANAGEMENT, BETHESDA, MARYLAND: “Anthropic’s IPO could provide a much-needed boost to sentiment across the AI ecosystem, as the offering is certainly generating considerable excitement among investors. However, enthusiasm for AI is increasingly competing with concerns about the rising cost of capital, particularly as some Federal Reserve policymakers are discussing the possibility of a 50-basis-point rate hike in December. A successful debut could lift sentiment, though sustaining that enthusiasm may be more difficult.“Over the next 6–12 months, the one indicator we would watch is AI stock market breadth relative to the broader technology sector. The volatility around AI is still frequently described as investor jitters rather than outright fear. In our view, the first sign that AI enthusiasm has peaked may not be a slowdown in AI spending, but the moment investors stop rewarding companies simply for being associated with AI.” MARK HACKETT, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, NATIONWIDE FINANCIAL, PHILADELPHIA: “Sentiment and positioning have shifted at a tremendous pace for the AI trade. It is no surprise that Anthropic is highly anticipated, as it is a leader, where the skepticism is more around the more speculative and risky crowd. How the AI space trades today will show if investors are committing new capital or simply reallocating funds from elsewhere. Strength among the competitors and complements would be an encouraging sign that the selloff is near the end, but weakness would tell a different story.” GIL LURIA, HEAD OF TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH, D.A. DAVIDSON, PORTLAND, OREGON: "Anthropic’s IPO is pivotal for the AI investment cycle. A successful IPO could extend the cycle by years and an unsuccessful IPO could stall investment. Indication that the IPO is shaping up well would be very positive for other AI-related stocks." JOE ZIDLE, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, CRESSET, NEW YORK: “Landmark IPOs tend to mark turning points in sentiment, so I interpret the success of ANT as an endorsement of the road ahead. Public investors are paying up, and that tells you that the debate has moved from ‘Is this real?’ to ‘Who captures the value?’ That’s a far healthier conversation for the whole AI ecosystem.”

Source: Reuters

TURIN, Nov 19 : World number four Ben Shelton had to battle for over two hours before carving out a 7-6(8) 7-5 win over Spaniard Rafael Jodar at the ATP Finals on Thursday to close in on a last four spot. The US Open finalist must wait for the result of the other group match later on Thursday between world number one Alexander Zverev, who has already made the semi-finals, and France's Arthur Fils. Nov 19 : Palo Alto Networks shares gained more than 6 per cent on Thursday as its higher annual forecast lifted cybersecurity stocks, with investors betting companies would spend big on defending against sophisticated AI-enabled cyberattacks. If the gains hold, Palo Alto would add more than $18 billion to its market value. Investor interest in cybersecurity firms has grown as AI reshapes the cyber arms race — the technology helps attackers uncover and exploit vulnerabilities faster, while increasing demand for software that can identify, block and respond to emerging threats before they multiply. Those concerns have been reinforced by a series of recent technology outages and vulnerabilities identified in Java and PHP, two programming languages underpinning millions of business applications and websites.

WASHINGTON, Nov 19 : NASA confirmed on Thursday that its Voyager 1 probe has achieved an unprecedented distance milestone — the first spacecraft to travel beyond a light-day from Earth — while flying into an uncertain future in interstellar space. The US space agency said it received a radio signal from the robotic explorer, launched in 1977, indicating that it passed the distance that light travels in 24 hours — about 16 billion miles (26 billion km) — as expected on Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object. NASA waited a day to make the official announcement because it took about that long for the spacecraft's signal to reach Earth. "Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets," Joe Westlake, director of NASA's heliophysics division, said in a statement released by the agency.

"But it went on to become central to NASA's fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the sun," Westlake said. Voyager 1 journeyed past Jupiter and Saturn, the solar system's two largest planets, earlier in its mission. It continues to gather scientific data. Voyager 1 is flying at almost 38,000 miles per hour (61,000 kph). It crossed the outer edge of the heliosphere, a protective bubble of particles and magnetic fields produced by the sun, to enter interstellar space in 2012. Its twin, Voyager 2, was also launched in 1977 and entered interstellar space in 2018. A representative at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory said this week that recent power-saving measures could give the two Voyager spacecraft enough power to stay in communication with Earth for three to four more years. Voyager 1 is still collecting data in the near-vacuum of interstellar space on effects from the sun such as solar storms that cause shocks and pressure fronts that extend as far away as the probe's current location. The 50th anniversary of its launch is next year.

LISBON, Nov 19 : The burgeoning six-a-side Baller League said on Thursday that it will launch in 2027 its own Nations Cup tournament spanning 64 cities and 16 countries with $1 million each for the winning men's and women's teams. "We believe it is the biggest prize ever put up for amateur footballers,” Baller League CEO Felix Starck said in a statement. Founded in 2024 in Germany and now with leagues in the UK and the US, the Baller League offers audiences a glitzier, shorter and cheaper version of watching the so-called "Beautiful Game" compared to traditional 90-minute soccer. “Football is pricing out the people who made it. A ticket to the World Cup cost thousands of dollars,” said Starck, stressing how any team could aspire to win its Nations Cup.

The NBA Europe project and a rival Euroleague expansion plan are both targeting a 2027 launch, putting the two competitions on a potential collision course. Cardinale, a prospective NBA Europe franchise owner, said the NBA could succeed where the established Euroleague had struggled financially. "The Euroleague hasn’t been able to fund itself over 26 years," Cardinale told the Sports Business Journal Dealmakers Conference.

"It’s this fascinating confluence of longevity, brand and fan base, and yet the financial fundamentals haven’t kept pace with that." EUROLEAGUE POINTS TO REVENUE GROWTH Euroleague CFO Xavi Puyada said it had "consistently increased its revenues season after season, achieving fivefold growth in commercial revenues over the past decade. Tatum, who appeared alongside Cardinale on the panel, said the NBA remained on schedule to launch the competition in 2027. "The role of the fans and these teams in their communities is something that eclipses what we know in America," he said. "That’s very exciting. It’s totally income-inelastic. It is part of the fabric of the community." RedBird is also the majority shareholder in football club AC Milan. Tatum said a basketball game between an AC Milan team and Real Madrid would have global appeal that NBA Europe could capitalise on. British broadcaster Sky News reported on Monday that the NBA was discussing an investment in an infrastructure fund for European basketball. WASHINGTON, Nov 19 : The rapid artificial intelligence buildout is putting upward pressure on US inflation through its impact on demand, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Thursday, with possible productivity gains that could help ease price pressures only coming "in the future." In prepared remarks to a Brazilian central bank conference, Jefferson said the AI boom is the sort of shock that could influence both demand and supply, but at different points in time. "On the demand side, optimism about the technology has been boosting business investment in data centers, advanced computing equipment, and related products," Jefferson said. "Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation." Productivity improvements from the new technology could put downward pressure on prices, but only "in the future," Jefferson said, without estimating a timeline. Jefferson's prepared remarks did not mention his current interest-rate outlook. The Fed is expected to raise its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point from the current range of 3.75 per cent-4.00 per cent at its December 8-9 policy meeting.

Source: Reuters

BANGKOK, Nov 19 : FIFA chief Gianni Infantino handed out trophies at the Asian Football Confederation annual awards on Thursday, including to Iran goalkeeper Alireza Beiranvand as AFC Player of the Year, hours after he was confirmed as running for reelection. The 56-year-old Infantino will face a challenge from French Football Federation boss Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association Honorary President - and FIFA Council member - Kozo Tashima for the FIFA presidency in Rabat on March 18. Infantino was widely criticised over his FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal to bring private investment into a new entity controlling commercial rights linked to major FIFA competitions, including the World Cup. He subsequently abandoned the project and apologised over the way it was handled at a closed FIFA Council meeting.

The Swiss met a number of global soccer's powerbrokers at the awards in Thailand, including AFC President Sheikh Salman. Beiranvand received his trophy from Infantino and Sheikh Salman. North Korea's Kim Kyong Yong won the women's award. FIRST KEEPER HONOURED The 34-year-old Beiranvand is the first keeper to win the trophy since it was introduced in 1994 and the fifth Iranian named the continent's best player, following Khodadad Azizi, Ali Daei, Mehdi Mahdavikia and Ali Karimi. He was recognised for his performances at club level with Tractor FC and for the national team. "Receiving this award is an incredibly historic, unforgettable and emotional moment in my life," said Beiranvand.  "But above all I feel an immense sense of happiness and pride in representing my country. I do not see this award as an individual achievement. It is an honour that belongs to the people of Iran." Beiranvand won the men's award ahead of Saudi Arabian duo Feras Al-Brikan and Salem Al-Dawsari and was recognised for his performances at the World Cup, where Iran narrowly missed out on a place in the knockout rounds. Kim became the second player from North Korea to win the women's award after being recognised for her performances in Naegohyang FC's title-winning campaign in the Asian Women's Champions League. "Now that I have got this award, my dream has come true," she said.  Go Kuroda was named men's coach of the year after steering Japan's Machida Zelvia to the Asian Champions League Elite final, where they lost to the Matthias Jaissle-coached Al-Ahli of Saudi Arabia. Iran's Marziyeh Jafari retained the women's coaching award for her work with Bam Khatoon in the Asian Women's Champions League. South Korea's Lee Kang-in was the men's International Player of the Year after featuring for Paris Saint-Germain in their Champions League triumph this year, while Australia's Caitlin Foord won the women's award, having claimed the Champions Cup with Arsenal.

Source: Reuters
